messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — KV cache continuous-batching regression detected. Metric anomalies: kv.evictions +420%, kv.kv_cache_size_bytes +300% across region-us-west-2, request error-rate elevated for batch endpoints. Suggested severity: P2. Paging on-call: @Alex Chen. Links: https://console.redwood/alerts/1765432100
Alex Chen: I'm on it. seeing the alert, jumping into dashboards. can someone drop recent deploys?
deploy-bot: Recent deploys: eng-runtime/branch/batch-window-optimizations -> deployed 1765429000 to us-west-2, canary 10%
Alex Chen: thanks. initial hypothesis: new kernel change + continuous batching interactions causing large KV writes / cache churn. Priya, Marco — tagging you for perf graphs and eviction patterns.
Priya Rao: looking at kv evictions by tenant. There's a sharp spike around 1765430000. Top offenders: tenant:cust-219 (30% of ops), tenant:cust-88 (12%). It looks per-tenant concentrated, not global config.
Marco Diaz: checked node-level metrics: p95 GPU memory for serving nodes in shard-group-7 jumped from 60% -> 92%. Eviction churn aligns. continuous_batcher logs show repeated prefix inserts.
Li Wang: I can attach a live trace. Running: `kubectl -n inference logs -l app=batcher --tail=200` returning repeated `KVCache: insert loop: prefix_size=0x2000, new_entries=1024` entries.
Alex Chen: Good signal. We need an immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle continuous batching for affected shards/tenants 2) per-customer override to revert to legacy non-continuous mode for top tenants 3) temporary increase in eviction threshold as safety valve. Who can flip the flag for per-customer override?
Priya Rao: I can flip the runtime flag per-tenant via the admin API: `POST /admin/flags/tenant/{tenant_id}`. Recommend starting with cust-219 and cust-88. We'll canary with cust-219 only first.
Alex Chen: Do it. Keep a 10-min watch. Also create a canary policy: enable override on 1 shard (not whole region) then escalate.
Priya Rao: calling it now. `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://admin.redwood/flags/tenant/cust-219 -d '{"batcher.continuous":false,"reason":"eviction-surge-176543"}'`
Priya Rao: response 200. flag applied to tenant cust-219 -> routed to shard-group-7.
Marco Diaz: seeing drop in insert rate for cust-219 within 30s. kv.insert_rate_cust_219: 4800/s -> 600/s. GPU mem for shard-group-7 dropping to 74%. Good.
Alex Chen: Nice. Priya, after 10m, if stable, we should rollout to cust-88 and then do broader rollout (with 5% shard slices) until region stable.
Priya Rao: ack. scheduling sequential updates: cust-88 in 12m.
Sarah Nguyen: I’ll draft a customer ops note for cust-219 and cust-88 in case we need to call them. Short note: "We observed elevated serving latency on batch endpoints, applied a temporary routing override. No data loss. We will follow up."
Li Wang: Posting a couple of log snippets for the triage channel:
```
[2026-05-12T14:07:45Z] KVCache.insert tenant=cust-219 prefix=abc123 entries=1024 total_size=1.2GB
[2026-05-12T14:07:46Z] continuous_batcher.emit shard=sg-7 loop=fast backpressure=false
[2026-05-12T14:08:01Z] Eviction triggered tenant=cust-219 evicted=850 entries
```
Alex Chen: Can we also add a temporary global batcher throttle gate as backup? I can push a quick toggle to reduce max_batch_size while we stabilize. Reducing from 2048 -> 512 might cut surge.
Priya Rao: I'll prepare the flag change but prefer targeting affected shards first. If we see continued global pressure we escalate to global gate.
Marco Diaz: Noted. Also, we should pin the runtime branch causing Kernel changes on canary nodes to rollback if needed. Which nodes are running that deploy?
deploy-bot: Canary nodes for eng-runtime/batch-window-optimizations: node-7a, node-7b (10% traffic).
Alex Chen: Let's cordon node-7a and node-7b from canary traffic after we confirm canary correlation. Marco, do you want to trigger a rollback of that canary?
Marco Diaz: I want one more data point: compare eviction counts on canary vs non-canary nodes over last 15m. Pulling `promql`: `sum(rate(kv_evictions_total[15m])) by(node,deploy)`
Marco Diaz: result: canary nodes show 5.2x eviction rate vs baseline. OK, that’s convincing. I'll rollback the canary.
Marco Diaz: initiating rollback: `deployctl rollback --service eng-runtime --to-stable --region us-west-2`
deploy-bot: Rollback job queued: id=rb-1765432155. Expected completion ~2m.
Alex Chen: While rollback in progress, continue per-tenant mitigations. Priya, go ahead with cust-88 after confirmation window.
Priya Rao: cust-88 flag change posted. `200 OK`. Monitoring.
Marco Diaz: rollback complete, canary traffic reverted. Observed eviction rates starting to decline on the canary nodes.
Li Wang: Post-rollback metrics: region kv.evictions_total rate down ~65% from peak. GPU memory p95 back to ~68% region-wide.
Alex Chen: Good. Now we need to coordinate a controlled rollout of a hotfix for batch config and a safer default for continuous batching parameters. Proposals: - tighten continuous_batcher window (max_prefix_entries from 4096 -> 1024) - add tenant-level admission control defaults - add per-shard soft-limits and backoff
Priya Rao: I can prepare the config patch. Recommend alpha rollout to 5% shards, watch for 30m, then ramp.
Marco Diaz: Also add a short-lived metric alert for `kv.evictions > 50/s` per shard to catch regressions faster.
Sarah Nguyen: I'll prepare a customer status update and coordinate with Account Execs for the two most affected customers. Draft: "We applied an emergency override and rollback; we're implementing a fix and will follow up with timeline." Send for review?
Alex Chen: Yes. Keep messaging minimal and factual.
Priya Rao: Pushing hotfix branch: `git push origin batcher-hotfix-176543` -> CI kicks off. Running unit + perf quick checks.
deploy-bot: CI passed. Ready to canary: `deployctl canary --service eng-runtime --image batcher-hotfix:176543 --percent 5 --region us-west-2`
Alex Chen: Start canary to 5% shards. Monitor: eviction rate, insert rate, p99 latency.
Marco Diaz: Canary started. After 10m, early signs: insert_rate smoothing, max_prefix_sizes capped.
Li Wang: Observability: dashboard link https://console.redwood/dashboards/kv-batcher-hotfix for on-call watch.
Alex Chen: If metrics hold for 30m, plan to ramp to 20% then 100% by progressive rollout over 2-3 hours. If any tenant shows >2x baseline evictions, pause and rollback to previous stable.
Priya Rao: Canary at 5% -> 10m stable. Ramping to 20%.
Marco Diaz: 20% -> stable after 15m. Ramping to 50% with automated guardrails.
Alex Chen: Reminder: ensure per-tenant overrides remain available for immediate mitigation. Don't remove those hooks.
Sarah Nguyen: Sent internal incident summary to #customer-ops and drafted customer messages for the two tenants. Will coordinate outbound comms.
Priya Rao: 100% rollout complete. All regions showing normalized eviction rates and stable latencies.
Alex Chen: Great work. Post-incident actions: - RCAs: deep dive on interaction between kernel change and continuous batching algorithm - Add unit/integration test for prefix churn - Add canary guard comparing eviction deltas before allowing kernel changes - Make per-tenant override a documented on-call runbook step
Marco Diaz: I'll own the RCA and the canary guard change. Priya, please own the runbook update and the config hardening.
Priya Rao: ack. I'll open follow-up tickets and assign.
Alex Chen: Closing the incident alert in 30m if metrics don't regress. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Alert status: resolved -> condition cleared at 1765435600.
Alex Chen: Closing thread — leaving notes in the postmortem template.
